title: THE RICH GET RICHER: DISPARATE IMPACT OF SEMI-SUPERVISED LEARNING
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure any aspects related to faith or religion. It measures the disparate impact of Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) algorithms on different sub-populations, using demographic groups like race and gender as examples.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its primary finding is that Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) methods can have a disparate impact on different sub-populations, where groups with higher baseline accuracy ('the rich') benefit more than groups with lower baseline accuracy ('the poor'), a phenomenon termed the 'Matthew effect'. The sub-populations analyzed were based on class labels, race, and gender, not religion.
